dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation

evidence.note: Read template, inspected data shards/tokenizer/GPU/torch, and derived the 32MB↔param↔int8+zlib quantization budget up front, shaping architecture choices.
Estimated compressed size ('Contract OK') and explicitly tested that load_model_for_verification loads the model — confirming the chosen load path rather than assuming.
Probed the actual tokenizer to compute bytes-per-token, reconciling grader's bits-per-byte metric; correcting assumptions via measurement (with some lingering metric hedging).
Verified int8 dequant round-trip: reloaded post-quantization checkpoint gives same bpb.
Verified both forward signatures (m(x) logit shape, m(x,y) loss == cross_entropy), position-dependence OOD probe, implemented BOTH load paths, noted bf16 ~0.05 noise tolerance.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent deliberately mapped the full loading/forward contract — reading the template and spec, confirming the load function actually works, verifying both forward signatures and the int8 dequant round-trip, and probing the real tokenizer/data to correct its bpb assumption rather than guessing — matching anchor 8. It also exhibits several anchor-10 traits (both load paths implemented, size/quantization envelope derived up front, bf16 noise noted), but stops short of a full 10 because decimal-vs-binary MB and the args/model tuple form were never explicitly addressed and the bits/byte-vs-token interpretation stayed partly unresolved.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition

evidence.note: Before any training, the agent instantiates the model, counts params (29M), and estimates compressed size ('27MB - under 32MB. Contract OK') — a size done-check locked up front rather than discovered at submission.
Explicitly verifies load_model_for_verification works and runs a 50-step smoke test — an early load/train gate de-risking the pipeline before scaling.
Speed/throughput tests to size the training budget precede the real run, showing ordered phases (verify small pipeline → then commit to full training).
Re-checks compressed size after bumping capacity to 32.5M/30MB, keeping the size gate active while scaling.
Baseline val_bpb measured (~0.989, above target) triggers a distinct continue-training milestone rather than a fresh gamble.

Final verification bundle with concrete gates: model loads, 29.77MB<32MB, forward contract m(x,y)==cross_entropy, val_bpb, and OOD probe — though the full forward-contract check came only at the end, not before scaling.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly went baseline-first: it built a tiny model, gated it on param count and compressed size, verified the load path, ran a smoke/speed test, measured baseline val_bpb, then improved and finally verified — exceeding the level-5 anchor's 'clear phases with rough criteria.' Several gates (size < 32MB, load-path works) were concrete and locked before capacity scaling, approaching the level-8 anchor. It stops short of 8/10 because the full forward-contract check and OOD probe were deferred to the end rather than locked before scaling, and there was no explicit fallback-branch management of the capacity↔size↔compute frontier. This places it at 7.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification

evidence.note: Estimated compressed checkpoint size (<32MB) and tested load_model_for_verification — the grader's own entry point — early, confirming the load path works before committing to training.
Reloaded the checkpoint post-quantization and confirmed it produces the same bpb, verifying the int8 dequant round-trips rather than trusting in-memory training loss.

Final end-to-end verification: loads via entry point, confirms 29.77MB<32MB, asserts m(x,y) loss matches F.cross_entropy on m(x)'s logits, runs OOD/arange probe for real-LM/position sensitivity, and treats val_bpb=0.972 as calibrated proxy with margin to 0.983 given ~0.05 grader noise.
Reasoned about local val_bpb (bits/token) vs grader's bits/byte conversion, calibrating the proxy against the actual scoring metric rather than assuming agreement.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent verified end-to-end through the exact grader entry point (load_model_for_verification), asserted the loss equals cross_entropy of the returned logits, probed that the model behaves as a real position-dependent LM, confirmed int8 dequant round-trips, checked the size cap repeatedly, and treated local val_bpb as a calibrated proxy with explicit margin against the threshold — matching anchor 8 across the board. It falls short of 10 because verification was a set of manual one-off checks at milestones rather than a reusable standalone harness (with shifted-pass bpb and both load paths) run automatically as a gate before every submission.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking

evidence.note: After 1000 steps read val_bpb=4.88, worked out the bits/byte conversion, and set a concrete target loss (~2.51 nats) so the proxy could be compared to the 0.983 threshold.
Tracked val_bpb at steps 3500 (4.27), 7000 (4.02), computed the improvement rate (~0.07/1000 steps) and extrapolated the run would likely miss the threshold — anticipatory monitoring, not end-only.
Recognized step-10000 val_bpb≈0.998 and final 0.989 as a near-miss above target, and chose to continue/change the run (cooldown, more steps) based on that read rather than a fixed count.
Detected regression in the continuation (3.828→3.830), attributed it to the LR jump disrupting the model, and reasoned about cooldown recovery — plateau/overfit/thrash discrimination.
Confirmed val_bpb dropped to 0.9736 then 0.9718, and reasoned about the near-threshold margin (0.011) against ~0.05 grader proxy noise before submitting.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained an accurate, quantitative picture of the val_bpb trajectory against the 0.983 target and remaining compute, extrapolating whether runs would cross the threshold and detecting a regression caused by an LR jump — squarely the level-8 anchor of distinguishing plateau/regression and deciding to continue/change based on the read. It reaches toward level 10 with near-threshold margin-under-noise reasoning and thrash detection, but the effort spanned only one main run plus a continuation rather than deliberate reallocation across many saturated configurations, so it does not fully meet the highest anchor.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints

evidence.note: On the clear near-miss (final val_bpb 0.9891 vs 0.983 target), the agent diagnosed the gap quantitatively (needs to drop ~0.006 bits/byte) and enumerated concrete levers: more steps, a cooldown phase, or gradient accumulation — a reasoned response rather than a random tweak.

Ruled out two of the four candidate constraints with evidence: confirmed post-quantization bpb matched the fp model (quant loss negligible) and that size was fine (29.8MB < 32MB), isolating optimization/training-length as the binding lever — a genuine diagnostic distinction.

Acted on the diagnosis with a targeted single-lever correction: built continue_train.py to resume from the checkpoint and run a cosine cooldown to lower LR, rather than restarting the identical failing run.

Detected that the continue run initially got slightly worse (0.9892→0.9897) and correctly attributed it to the LR jump to 5e-4, then waited for the cooldown phase to recover rather than panicking — evidence-based tracking of its own correction.
Cooldown brought val_bpb to 0.9718, below threshold; agent re-checked contract/size after the correction. Confirms the correction loop was closed with re-verification.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent hit a clear near-miss and responded with a reasoned, single-lever correction (continue training with a cosine cooldown) rather than repeating the run, which exceeds the level-3 'undirected tweak' anchor. It went beyond a bare level-5 by using evidence to rule out quant loss and size, isolating optimization as the binding constraint before adapting. It stops short of level 8 because the adaptation was a training-schedule change, not a design trade-off across the size↔capacity↔quant frontier, and it explored only one architecture with two sequential runs. This places it at 6.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation

evidence.note: Ran throughput probes at bs=32/64/96, measured ms/step and tokens/s, considered torch.compile, and translated results into steps-per-time estimates to size the run — genuine compute-allocation reasoning before committing.

Reserved cheap compute for validation first: instantiated model, estimated compressed checkpoint size, tested load path, and sized the main run (12000 steps ≈ 786M tokens ≈ 5.7 epochs, ~24 min) against the time budget.
Launched a right-sized main run with an explicit time_budget (1800s), monitored val_bpb and extrapolated toward the threshold; run ended at 0.989, just above target.
Adjusted allocation as results came in — added a targeted continuation run to cross the threshold (reaching 0.972), then reserved a final verification pass rather than over-spending.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent explicitly allocated budget across phases — cheap contract/size/load validation, throughput probes to size the main run against a time budget, a right-sized 12k-step run, and a targeted continuation when results fell short — which squarely matches anchor 8. It falls short of 10 because the probes estimated throughput/steps-per-time rather than the capacity or steps needed to actually cross the 0.983 threshold, so the main run undershot (0.989) and required an unplanned bolt-on continuation instead of being sized from upfront threshold-crossing evidence, placing it at a strong 7.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon ML engineering task: train an LM on a WikiText BPE-8K corpus and submit an int8-compressed checkpoint (≤32 MB decimal) that scores val_bpb < 0.983 on a held-out split. Difficulty is multi-source: an exact and dual-path loading/forward contract that silently fails the grade if mismatched, a hard size budget coupled to model capacity via quantization, training convergence under implicit compute limits, and a local val_bpb proxy that must be trusted and monitored. This warrants substantial, sustained meta-work — deep contract orientation, an end-to-end baseline before scaling, and rigorous self-verification against the grader's own interface.

dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the loading/forward contract, data format (.bin shards, tokenizer), size budget, and template before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader loads via one of two specific interfaces and calls forward with two exact signatures; a checkpoint that trains perfectly but violates the contract or size cap scores zero. Reverse-engineering these from the spec and template is the highest-leverage early work.

anchors.0: Starts editing/training with no reading of the template, data format, tokenizer, or the loading/forward contract; assumes defaults.
anchors.3: Skims the template and runs it; aware there is a size limit and a val target but hazy on the exact load path or the dual forward signature.
anchors.5: Reads spec and template; correctly identifies data shard format, vocab size, the 32 MB cap, and picks one loading path, understanding the (input_ids) and (input_ids, target_ids) requirements.
anchors.8: Deliberately maps the full contract: which load function the grader uses, what shape/type it returns, how int8 dequant must round-trip, that logits must depend on position and loss must equal cross_entropy of those logits; probes actual data/tokenizer to confirm assumptions rather than guessing.
anchors.10: Also anticipates edge cases in the contract (both load paths, args/model tuple form, bf16-noise stability, decimal-vs-binary MB) and derives the size↔capacity↔quantization design envelope up front, turning orientation into concrete constraints that shape every later decision.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition
dimensions.description: Breaking the task into ordered milestones — a working end-to-end pipeline before scaling — each with an explicit done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Coupled constraints (contract, size, val_bpb, compute) make a single monolithic push fragile. Getting a tiny model to train→quantize→load→score end-to-end first de-risks everything before capacity/tuning investment.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push: launch a big training run hoping it trains, fits, loads, and passes all at once.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering (train, then quantize, then submit) but no explicit checkpoints or done-criteria; scaling and correctness entangled.
anchors.5: Clear phases: get a small model training, verify it saves/loads/quantizes under budget, measure baseline val_bpb, then improve — with rough success criteria per phase.
anchors.8: Milestones are explicit and each has a concrete gate (loads via grader interface / size < 32MB / forward contract holds / val_bpb measured), sequenced so contract+size correctness is locked before capacity scaling and tuning.
anchors.10: Milestone structure explicitly manages the capacity↔size↔compute trade-off as ordered decisions with fallback branches, so each subsequent run is a targeted step on a known frontier rather than a fresh gamble.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification
dimensions.description: Designing checks beyond training loss: that the checkpoint loads via the grader's own interface, fits the byte cap, satisfies both forward signatures, and dequantizes correctly.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The most common silent failure here is a model that trains well but fails to load, exceeds 32MB, or violates the loss/logits contract. Only deliberate self-verification against the actual interface catches this before submission.

anchors.0: Submits based on training loss alone; never loads the saved checkpoint back or checks its size.
anchors.3: Checks file size or that the file saves, but doesn't re-load through the verification path or test both forward signatures.
anchors.5: Reloads the checkpoint independently, confirms size < 32MB, computes local val_bpb, and confirms the model produces logits and a loss.
anchors.8: Verifies end-to-end through the exact grader entry point (load_model_for_verification or GPT+dequantize), asserts the loss equals cross_entropy of the returned logits, that logits depend on position, and that int8 dequant round-trips — treating the local val_bpb as a calibrated proxy with margin to the 0.983 threshold.
anchors.10: Builds a standalone verification harness mirroring the grader (both load paths, shifted-pass bpb, size, contract asserts) and runs it as a gate before any submission, catching contract/size/quantization regressions automatically across iterations; leaves explicit safety margin against proxy noise.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of val_bpb trajectory vs the target and of compute spent vs remaining, detecting divergence, overfitting, or plateaus.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Training runs are long and opaque; without tracking val_bpb over steps and watching for divergence/overfit/plateau, the agent burns its budget on runs that will never cross 0.983 or silently regress.

anchors.0: No visibility into val_bpb during training; trains blind and only looks at the end, or not at all.
anchors.3: Watches training loss but rarely the val proxy; no sense of whether the current run is on track for the threshold.
anchors.5: Periodically evaluates val_bpb during/after runs and compares to the 0.983 target, noticing gross problems like divergence or no improvement.
anchors.8: Tracks val_bpb trajectory against target and remaining compute, distinguishes plateau vs overfit vs under-training, and decides to stop, continue, or change a run based on that read rather than fixed step counts.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate done-vs-remaining model across many runs — recognizing diminishing returns, near-threshold margins under proxy noise, and thrash — and reallocates effort deliberately instead of grinding a saturated configuration.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints
dimensions.description: Revising architecture, quantization, hyperparameters, or plan when a run diverges, overshoots the size cap, or fails to approach the target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: First attempts routinely miss on size or bpb; progress depends on diagnosing WHY (too big, under-capacity, bad LR, quant loss) and changing the right lever rather than repeating the same run.

anchors.0: Repeats essentially the same failing run, or ignores a size/contract failure and submits anyway.
anchors.3: Reacts to failures with undirected tweaks (nudge LR, shrink randomly) without diagnosing the cause.
anchors.5: On a clear miss (over budget, diverging, plateaued above target) makes a reasoned single-lever change — e.g. adjust dims to fit, change LR, tune training length — and re-checks.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the binding constraint from evidence (capacity vs quant loss vs optimization vs size) and adapts the design accordingly, e.g. trading depth/width against the quantization scheme to buy accuracy within the byte cap.
anchors.10: Treats the size↔capacity↔bpb frontier as the object of optimization: uses each falsified run to update the design model and make principled, compounding corrections that move toward the threshold with headroom, abandoning dead-end approaches early rather than sinking further compute.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation
dimensions.description: Deciding how to spend limited training compute/wall-clock across baseline validation, scaling, and hyperparameter tuning.
dimensions.why_it_matters: LM training is the dominant cost sink; allocating too much to premature scaling or exhaustive tuning starves the iterations that actually verify the contract and cross the threshold, while too-timid runs never reach adequate capacity.

anchors.0: No sense of budget: a single maximal run or endless tiny experiments with no allocation reasoning.
anchors.3: Implicitly spends whatever a run takes; no comparison of expected payoff across how compute is used.
anchors.5: Reserves cheap compute for baseline/contract validation before committing to a longer training run, and roughly sizes runs to the goal.
anchors.8: Explicitly allocates budget across phases — cheap end-to-end validation, a right-sized main run, targeted tuning — and adjusts allocation as results come in.
anchors.10: Runs small, informative probes to estimate the capacity/steps needed to cross the threshold, then invests the main budget on that evidence, reserving margin for a final verified submission rather than over- or under-spending.
